gen-dafont-outrun-future-gf-sulphur-poin: Sulphur Point sets down bulky lowercase with generous gaps in its a, c, e and s, marker-like and easy to follow. Sulphur Point's steady line meets Outrun Future, a wide-stanced synthwave heading whose outline never changes width, so a full page keeps moving without a snag.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Heavy, bold Plakkaat curls its terminals round until they nearly touch the stem, closed up tight. And Anek Gurmukhi answers with big open counters in every small letter, which leaves the heading free to work large and brief.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-anek-latin: Plakkaat looks like bent straw turned into letters, every stroke cut with one fixed nib width and the curls nearly closing. But Anek Latin keeps its tall lowercase reaching toward the capitals, held open instead of curled shut, and does its best work in running text.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-anek-malayalam: Bold and heavy, Plakkaat looks like solder pulled through a nozzle, every stroke thick and close to its capitals in height. Anek Malayalam is the quieter worker, with clean curves whose tips never touch, built for the text itself while the heading takes the shouting.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-anek-odia: Heavy lettering leads here, with Plakkaat joints that never thin or bulge. Anek Odia follows with unlatched rounds and capitals barely above lowercase, so the thick heading and the light, open text sit together without crowding.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-anuphan: Terminals that sweep round to almost touch the stem give Plakkaat its closed, bent-straw look. Anuphan opens everything back up with big round lowercase bowls and clear gaps, and that closed-versus-open split is what makes the pair.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-armata: Plakkaat is heavy and closed, with a y whose tail is as thick as its arm and terminals curling toward the stem. Armata, spacious and open, takes over below it, and the heading is best kept big and short.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-athiti: Plakkaat is heavy, closed and bent-straw round. Athiti reads like sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width, with see-through s shapes and a high mean line that keep a long passage moving smoothly beneath the weighty heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-atkinson-hyperleg: Approachable is the right word for the body here, though the heading is the loud one, with Plakkaat curves and straights sharing a single width. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next puts washer-big eyes in its lowercase and leaves its rounds unlatched, so the two sit side by side as heavy and open.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-fresca: Modern and clean is the body's side of the story, with Fresca keeping its counters connected to the outside and no calligraphic thinning. Fresca's short ascenders over big bowls meet Plakkaat's closed, heavy curls, and that open-versus-closed gap is the pair's strongest single quality.
